annotation_description: Gem25P Tinker missed their Turn 1 land drop entirely despite having 4 lands in hand (Command Tower, Dragonskull Summit, Swamp, Temple of Malice). This resulted in being forced to discard during cleanup and falling a full turn behind on mana development in a format where early ramp is critical.

Fetched Forest when they already have abundant green sources (Forest on battlefield, Forest in hand, Necroblossom Snarl). Blue is their scarcest color with only Command Tower producing it, and their commander Galea requires U. An Island would provide redundancy for their most critical missing color.

Playing Flood Plain (enters tapped) instead of Exotic Orchard (enters untapped) wastes the entire turn 4 with no spells cast. Exotic Orchard would provide a third mana, enabling Swiftfoot Boots (2 mana) to be cast this turn with 1 mana left over for Brainstorm.

Cast Swiftfoot Boots with no creatures on the battlefield. The reasoning incorrectly claims there's a 3/3 Elemental to protect, but no creatures exist on MiniMx's board. While Boots can prepare for a future Galea cast, activating Flood Plain to fetch a basic land could accelerate reaching 5 mana for Galea (which costs {1}{G}{W}{U}) sooner.

Spending 3 mana (2R) and tapping Shivan Gorge to deal 1 damage to each opponent is extremely inefficient at this stage of the game. With 40 life opponents, dealing 1 damage is negligible. Meanwhile, Gem25P Tinker has Oketra's Monument and Kari Zev in hand that could be cast to develop the board. The 3 mana spent on Shivan Gorge's ability plus the mana from other lands could have been used to cast Oketra's Monument (3 mana) to set up future cost reduction and token generation, which would have been far more impactful. Additionally, tapping Shivan Gorge means it can't produce colorless mana for other uses this turn.

Fetched Island when Plains would better support the hand's mana requirements. The player already has Prairie Stream for Blue and has Halimar Depths and Lumbering Falls in hand for additional Blue. Meanwhile, Valiant Endeavor requires {W}{W} and the player only has Canopy Vista and Prairie Stream for White. A Plains would also help ensure future dual lands with basic land requirements enter untapped.

With Galea as commander (who casts Aura/Equipment from top of library), Halimar Depths' ability to arrange the top 3 cards is extremely synergistic and valuable. Since MiniMx Memoir appears to have no meaningful plays with remaining mana this turn, the tempo cost of a tapped land is negligible. Grasslands is also arguably better as it provides future ramp when cracked.

Gem25P Tinker passed on activating Shivan Gorge ({2}{R}, {T}: deal 1 damage to each opponent) during combat when they had the mana available (Command Tower, Dragonskull Summit, Temple of Malice, Fellwar Stone, Shivan Gorge itself for colorless, plus Mobilized District). This is a free damage ability with no downside - 1 damage to all three opponents for 3 mana at instant speed. Additionally, they then had to discard Oketra's Monument and Ambition's Cost to hand size, losing significant card advantage. The discard of Ambition's Cost (draw 3 cards) and Oketra's Monument (cost reduction + token generation) represents substantial lost value. While discarding was forced by the hand size limit, they could have at minimum used Shivan Gorge to spend mana productively, and the choice to discard Ambition's Cost over other cards like Geier Reach Sanitarium is questionable since Ambition's Cost provides much more card advantage.

Psychic Impetus was cast targeting a 1/1 Human Soldier Token controlled by MiMo Gramps. This makes the token a 3/3 goaded creature that must attack someone other than MiniMx Memoir. However, MiMo Gramps has Omen of the Sun and could sacrifice it or the token could easily be blocked and killed. More importantly, putting an Aura on a 1/1 token is extremely risky - tokens are fragile and if the token dies, the Aura is lost for no value. Psychic Impetus is much better on a larger, harder-to-remove creature like The Peregrine Dynamo (1/5 body, harder to kill in combat) which would force Gem25P Tinker to attack others while giving MiniMx Memoir scry 2 triggers. The reasoning stated in the decision ('gives card draw when enchanted creature dies') is factually wrong about what the card does - it gives +2/+2, goads, and scries on attack. The player misread their own card.

MiniMx Memoir cast Verdant Embrace targeting an opponent's Human Soldier Token (MiMo Gramps' creature), not their own creature. MiniMx Memoir has no creatures on the battlefield - only lands, Swiftfoot Boots, and Arcane Signet. Verdant Embrace is an Aura that enchants a creature, giving it +3/+3 and creating 1/1 Saproling tokens at each upkeep. By enchanting an opponent's creature, MiniMx Memoir is giving MiMo Gramps a 4/4 soldier and the Saproling token generation. The reasoning also confuses Verdant Embrace with a completely different card (it doesn't create 2/2 flying Spirit tokens). Since MiniMx Memoir has no creatures of their own, they should have held the Verdant Embrace until they could put it on their own creature, or played a land drop first (they have several lands in hand including Halimar Depths, Lumbering Falls, etc.) and used Vitu-Ghazi to make a Saproling token to enchant on a future turn.

With a hand of all lands and no spells, playing Forest provides no meaningful advantage over Halimar Depths, which would let them arrange the top 3 cards of their library to find action. The enters-tapped drawback of Halimar Depths is negligible when there are no spells in hand to cast this turn.

message: Select a player, planeswalker, or battle to attack
annotation_description: Attacking into KimiK2 Johnny who has Nin, the Pain Artist untapped with 8 available mana. KimiK2 could use Nin to deal 5 damage to The Peregrine Dynamo (killing the 1/5) and draw 5 cards, which would be a massive value swing. The 1 damage dealt is negligible compared to the risk.

message: Select a card ORDER to put on the BOTTOM of your library (last one chosen will be bottommost)
annotation_description: MiMo Gramps is scrying 2 (from sacrificing Omen of the Sun) and choosing which card to put on the bottom. They have Sigil of the Empty Throne and Dreadhorde Invasion as the two cards. With 8 lands on board (including Necroblossom Snarl and Command Tower for black), they could cast either card next turn. However, Sigil of the Empty Throne at 5 mana (3WW) is a powerful enchantment payoff that creates 4/4 flying Angels whenever they cast enchantment spells. They already have Arasta of the Endless Web and Spirited Companion in hand (both enchantments), plus Verdant Embrace is an enchantment in their deck. Sigil would generate significant value from their enchantment-heavy strategy. Dreadhorde Invasion is a 2-mana enchantment that slowly creates a growing Zombie Army token but costs 1 life per turn (they're already at 27 life). Keeping Sigil on top would be significantly better as it provides immediate synergy with their hand full of enchantments and generates much more impactful tokens (4/4 flyers vs slowly growing a single token). Bottoming Sigil in favor of Dreadhorde Invasion loses meaningful value.

Playing Bant Panorama over Halimar Depths is debatable. With a hand full of lands and only Eel Umbra as a spell, Halimar Depths would let MiniMx Memoir look at the top 3 cards and reorder them, potentially finding action cards instead of more land drops. Bant Panorama enters untapped and can be sacrificed later to fetch a basic, but they already have 8 lands on the battlefield and are flooding out. Halimar Depths' scry-like effect would help find spells to actually impact the board. However, Bant Panorama does provide immediate untapped colorless mana and a future land-thinning effect, so the choice isn't terrible.

Eel Umbra was cast targeting Vitu-Ghazi, the City-Tree, which is a land — not a creature. Vitu-Ghazi only becomes a creature when its activated ability resolves ({2}{G}{W}, {T}: Create a 1/1 green Saproling creature token — wait, actually Vitu-Ghazi creates tokens, it doesn't become a creature). Looking more carefully, Vitu-Ghazi is just a land that makes Saproling tokens. It is never a creature. Eel Umbra requires 'Enchant creature' so it cannot legally enchant Vitu-Ghazi. Even if the game engine allowed this, it's wasting a card on a non-creature permanent. The player should have held Eel Umbra as a combat trick with flash for a future creature, or passed the turn.

Eel Umbra gives +1/+1 and umbra armor (destruction protection) to the enchanted creature. Putting it on a 1/1 Saproling token that MiniMx Memoir controls is a waste of a card with flash that could protect a much more valuable creature. The player has Setessan Champion (which draws cards from enchantments entering and grows with +1/+1 counters) and Kari Zev on the battlefield. Enchanting Setessan Champion would trigger Constellation (drawing a card and adding a +1/+1 counter), making it a 3/5, AND giving it destruction protection via umbra armor. Enchanting a Saproling token wastes the umbra armor protection on a disposable token and misses the Constellation trigger entirely.

message: Select a player, planeswalker, or battle to attack
annotation_description: Not selecting 'All attack' when attacking KimiK2 Johnny at 15 life. The Peregrine Dynamo (1/5) has virtually no risk attacking alongside Josu Vess since Johnny only has a 1/1 Merchant of Secrets as a potential blocker. Every point of damage matters when trying to eliminate a player.

message: Select an artifact, creature, or planeswalker
annotation_description: Gem25P Tinker had Bedevil on the stack but declined to use any activated abilities or pay for it, effectively letting Bedevil fizzle or not resolving properly. More importantly, they passed without playing Foreboding Ruins (a land from hand) which could have been played this turn since they have a Swamp to reveal. They also missed the opportunity to use Shivan Gorge's activated ability ({2}{R}, {T}: deal 1 damage to each opponent) when KimiK2 Johnny is at 7 life - though that's only 1 damage. The critical issue is that with Bedevil on the stack targeting something, they chose 'False' (declining to act), and the turn passed to MiMo Gramps, suggesting Bedevil may not have resolved properly or they missed using it optimally. Additionally, they didn't play their land (Foreboding Ruins) this turn, missing a land drop.

message: Select a card ORDER to put on the BOTTOM of your library (last one chosen will be bottommost)
annotation_description: Belt of Giant Strength is likely the stronger card to have closer to the top of the bottom cards - it's cheaper to cast (1G vs 4) and creates a much bigger threat (10/10) especially with creatures already on board. Clay Golem is just a 4/4 with an expensive activation. Though both are going to the bottom so impact is minimal.

The player chose to play Lumbering Falls (which enters tapped) instead of playing a land and using their mana more efficiently. However, the bigger issue is that they had Halimar Depths and Grasslands in hand as well. Lumbering Falls enters tapped and provides GU mana, but the player already has abundant GWU mana sources (8 lands + Arcane Signet). Grasslands could fetch a basic land (untapped) and thin the deck, while Halimar Depths would let them arrange the top 3 cards of their library. With no pressing need for the creature-land activation and plenty of mana already, Halimar Depths would have provided card selection to find relevant spells, which is more valuable at this stage of the game where the player has only 3 cards in hand (all lands) and needs to draw into action.

MiniMx Memoir incorrectly assessed they had insufficient mana to activate Lumbering Falls ({2}{G}{U}). They had Forest, Canopy Vista, Arcane Signet, and other sources available - more than enough. With only lands in hand and nothing else to spend mana on, a free 3 damage from a hexproof creature is value left on the table.

MiniMx Memoir has 8 lands in play (Canopy Vista, Prairie Stream, Vitu-Ghazi the City-Tree, Island, Exotic Orchard, Skycloud Expanse, Forest) plus Arcane Signet, and has Halimar Depths, Grasslands, and Island in hand. They should play a land this turn since they haven't yet (it's postcombat main). Additionally, Vitu-Ghazi the City-Tree's activation costs {2}{G}{W}{T} to create a 1/1 Saproling. With 7 lands + Arcane Signet, they likely have enough mana to activate it as a mana sink, creating a token. But more importantly, they need to play a land - Halimar Depths would let them set up future draws, or Grasslands could fetch a land later. Passing without playing a land is a missed land drop.

message: Pick triggered ability (goes to the stack first)
annotation_description: Copying Kari Zev's triggered ability creates a second legendary Ragavan token, but the legend rule forces you to immediately sacrifice one, netting zero additional attackers. Copying Captain Lannery Storm's Treasure trigger would have given an extra Treasure token (usable for mana and to pump Captain Lannery Storm +1/+0).

MiMo Gramps had enough mana to cast both Ondu Spiritdancer (5 mana) and Spirited Companion (2 mana) this turn with 7+ lands available. By casting Spirited Companion first (or instead), they missed the Ondu Spiritdancer trigger that would have created a token copy of Spirited Companion when it entered, netting an extra card draw and an extra 1/1 body.

message: Choose spell or ability to play: Lumbering Falls
chosen_display: 3. {2}{G}{U}: Lumbering Falls becomes a 3/3 green and blue Elemental creature with hexproof until end of turn. It's still a land.
annotation_description: MiniMx Memoir passed on activating Lumbering Falls during combat, missing the opportunity to attack with a 3/3 hexproof creature against Gem25P Tinker who has no blockers. With only lands in hand and no other plays, there's little reason not to use the mana to push 3 damage.

With only lands in hand and effectively in topdeck mode, playing a basic Island wastes the opportunity to use Halimar Depths to arrange the top 3 cards of the library. Since it's postcombat main, the 'enters tapped' drawback of Halimar Depths is negligible, and the card selection is very valuable when the player has no spells in hand.

MiniMx Memoir activated Lumbering Falls' creature animation ability ({2}{G}{U}) during their own postcombat main phase, where the 3/3 hexproof creature can't attack (combat already happened) and will revert at end of turn. This wastes 4 mana for no benefit. The reasoning even says 'I'll select option 2' but chose option 3, suggesting a misclick or confused reasoning. Additionally, with Halimar Depths in hand and a land drop available, they should be playing that land to set up future draws.

message: Select a player, planeswalker, or battle to attack
annotation_description: Attacked Gem25P Tinker at 38 life who has potential blockers (Mobilized District can activate for 3 mana, Peregrine Dynamo is a 1/5) instead of MiniMx Memoir at 27 life who has zero creatures and cannot block at all.

message: Choose spell or ability to play: Bant Panorama
annotation_description: MiniMx Memoir tapped Bant Panorama for colorless mana during combat with no apparent use for it (no abilities to activate, no spells to cast in combat). They have 8 lands but only 4 cards in hand (Halimar Depths, Grasslands, Plains, Colossus Hammer) - none of which need mana during combat. Meanwhile, sacrificing Bant Panorama to fetch a basic land would thin the deck and provide a colored mana source for future turns. With only 8 lands and cards like Colossus Hammer (which costs 8 to equip), getting more lands onto the battlefield is important. The colorless mana generated during combat will likely go to waste.

Playing Plains over Halimar Depths in postcombat main when no immediate mana is needed. Halimar Depths entering tapped is free here since the turn is effectively over, and its scry-like effect (top 3 reorder) synergizes with Galea, Kindler of Hope's ability to cast Aura/Equipment from the top of library. Playing Plains now wastes the opportunity to get Halimar Depths' ETB tapped downside for free.

Activating Lumbering Falls for 4 mana ({2}{G}{U}) in postcombat main phase creates a 3/3 hexproof creature that can't attack this turn (combat is already over). The creature reverts to a land at end of turn, so this activation accomplishes nothing meaningful. The reasoning mentions 'effectively a 5/5 with previous activations' which doesn't make sense - Lumbering Falls becomes a 3/3, and there's no indication of any pump effects. This wastes 4 mana that could have been used for other purposes or saved.

The player's reasoning is based on a hallucinated game state - they believe Shanid is already on the battlefield when it's actually in their hand. This confusion about their own board state likely leads to suboptimal decision-making. Additionally, with 8 lands but no white mana sources, neither Shanid (1RWB) nor Arvad (3WB) can be cast, so the player should be focused on finding white mana or advancing their board with available plays like casting equipment (Tenza/Honor-Worn Shaku/Blackblade Reforged) or using Thrill of Possibility to dig for lands.

During combat, Gem25P Tinker had the opportunity to activate Shivan Gorge ({2}{R}, {T}) to deal 1 damage to each opponent (MiMo Gramps at 16hp, MiniMx Memoir at 27hp) for free chip damage, and potentially activate Mobilized District to create a 3/3 attacker. Instead, the AI appears to have timed out or made an incoherent choice, failing to utilize available activated abilities for value.

Casting Thrill of Possibility during combat gives MiMo Gramps a 1/2 Spider token from Arasta of the Endless Web, which is unnecessary. Thrill could have been cast at end of turn or at another time when Arasta wasn't on the battlefield or when the Spider token wouldn't matter. Additionally, discarding Arvad the Cursed - a strong legendary creature that gives other legendaries +2/+2 and has deathtouch/lifelink - is a significant cost. With Shanid already in hand as another legendary creature, Arvad could have been quite valuable if cast. The timing during combat (rather than end of opponent's turn) also means the Spider could potentially block if combat hasn't resolved yet.

Activated Lumbering Falls to become a 3/3 creature during postcombat main phase. Since combat is already over, the creature can't attack, and the animation wears off at end of turn (their own turn), so it provides no blocking benefit either. This spent {2}{G}{U} for absolutely no effect.

Failed to play Shizo, Death's Storehouse (a legendary land) before equipping Blackblade Reforged. Playing Shizo first would trigger Shanid's ability (draw a card, lose 1 life) and add an extra land to the battlefield, making Blackblade Reforged give +9/+9 instead of +8/+8. This is a sequencing error that loses both a card draw and +1/+1 on the equipped creature.

MiMo Gramps is at 3 HP with no creatures on the battlefield. After animating Lumbering Falls into a 3/3 hexproof creature, MiniMx Memoir skipped the attack phase entirely, missing lethal damage against MiMo Gramps.
